prompt:
Image 1 is a storyboard sheet of one scene of a Sri Lankan television drama: a grid of photorealistic film stills separated by thin white gutters. Paint again ONLY the masked panels listed below, each inside its own cell, in the same world as the rest of the sheet: the same place, light, weather, colour grade and mannequins. Everything outside the masked cells stays exactly as it is, the gutters too.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the storyboard sheet to edit; image 2 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 3 is the reference sheet for phone.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One painted storyboard image contains eleven panels in shot order, four across and three down, with the bottom-right cell empty. There are no written marks, labels, arrows or readable lettering anywhere. Kasun is a smooth red artist's mannequin and Anudi a smooth blue artist's mannequin, retaining their respective reference heights and builds; all human appearance details are replaced by this mannequin treatment. The setting and props are realistic: rain-wet Colombo asphalt, concrete pavement, an open kerb drain, weathered commercial buildings and a modest food three-wheeler beneath a faded blue canopy. Soft early-morning daylight comes from the open road at camera right, with subdued amber shop lamps beneath the canopy. Use muted greys, dusty beige, leaf-green accents and controlled wet reflections throughout. The smartphone has the reference orange back, transparent cover and three-camera cluster. Anudi holds the open navy umbrella in her left hand, with the tan handbag's short handles looped over her left forearm; her right hand receives and subsequently holds the phone.

Geography: The pavement forms a continuous left-to-right route beside the road, with the open drain running along its roadward edge. The food three-wheeler occupies the vending bay at the left, backed by shuttered shopfronts and the faded blue canopy. Kasun stands immediately right of that bay, screen left, facing Anudi, who stands screen right beside a stained cream boundary wall with a pale-green painted strip. Her departure route continues horizontally toward screen right along that wall, while the business remains to the left. Every camera stays on the roadward side of their conversational axis. Wider views retain the blue canopy at left and the cream-and-green wall at right; tighter views isolate the appropriate stretch of this same connected frontage.

PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Roadward side at waist height, looking slightly downward across Anudi's right hand; normal close-focus lens, tight insert of the hand and phone. Background: Only shallow-focus ground is visible: a dark strip of the kerb drain at lower left and wet concrete pavement toward frame right. The business and wall are outside the tight crop. The blue mannequin's right hand and the orange phone fill the panel, the fingers wrapped around the lower and side edges of the transparent case. The phone's orange back and three black camera circles face the camera; its display is angled away toward Anudi and is not visible. A soft dark strip of the kerb drain sits at lower left, with wet concrete filling the right background.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
